title: In what order do we work out an expression with many operations?
description: Three expressions with more than one operation are worked out in a fixed order: brackets, then multiplication, then adding or taking away. Keeko doubts this and wants to work from left to right.
teaching_notes: One idea: brackets come first, then multiplication, and then adding or taking away, and the parts that are added are called terms. Watch for students who work from left to right and so take away before they multiply.

video_script.why: A learner sees that an expression with more than one operation has one value only when the operations are done in a fixed order.
video_script.substitution: The book's own three expressions, worked out in the order brackets, multiplication, then adding or taking away.
video_script.anchor: three expressions, each with more than one operation
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko works left to right, so 23 minus 10 comes first and gives 13, then 13 times 2 gives 26, but multiplication must come first and the value is 3.
video_script.payoff_line: The three values are three, eighty two and one hundred

final_answer.spoken: the values are three, eighty two and one hundred

never_show: the three values together before the answer beat
maths_rules: Brackets first, then multiplication, then adding or taking away.
video_script.design: One idea: operations are done in a fixed order, so an expression has one value. Assumes products of numbers and the idea of a bracket. The three expressions stay on the stage with each step coloured. Wrong idea: work left to right.

narration: <bookmark mark='p1'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='p2'/>It gives three expressions, and each one has more than one operation.
<bookmark mark='p3'/>The operations are taking away, multiplying, adding and a bracket.
<bookmark mark='p4'/>In what order should we work them out?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: three steps on a ladder: brackets first, then multiplication, then adding or taking away; a sample expression with its parts circled and the word term written under one part

marks.g1: a ladder with three steps appears
marks.g2: the steps are labelled brackets, multiplication, adding or taking away
marks.g3: a part of an expression is circled and the word term is written under it

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>When an expression has many operations, the order matters, so we follow a fixed order.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>Brackets come first, then multiplication, and then adding or taking away.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>Each part of an expression that is added or taken away is called a term.

marks.gv2: the second expression is written under it
marks.gv3: the third expression is written under that

narration: <bookmark mark='gv1'/>Given, the first expression is twenty three minus ten times two.
<bookmark mark='gv2'/>The second is seven times four plus nine times six.
<bookmark mark='gv3'/>The third is twenty plus eight times the bracket sixteen minus six.

beats.on_screen: To find: the value of each expression
narration: <bookmark mark='fd1'/>We find the value of each expression by working in the right order.

marks.s1a: the two terms 23 and −10 × 2 are circled
marks.s1b: 10 × 2 is worked out first and becomes 20

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>In the first expression, the terms are twenty three and minus ten times two.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>Multiplication comes first, so ten times two is twenty.
<bookmark mark='s1c'/>Taking twenty away from twenty three leaves three.

marks.s2a: the two products 7 × 4 and 9 × 6 are circled

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>In the second expression, both products come before the adding.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>Seven times four is twenty eight, and nine times six is fifty four.
<bookmark mark='s2c'/>Twenty eight plus fifty four is eighty two.

marks.s3a: the bracket 16 − 6 is worked out first and becomes 10

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>In the third expression, the bracket is worked first, so sixteen minus six is ten.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>Then eight times ten is eighty.
<bookmark mark='s3c'/>Last, twenty plus eighty is one hundred.

marks.ans: the three values are boxed together

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The three values are three, eighty two and one hundred.
Each value needed the right order of operations.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 23 − 10 = 13, then 13 × 2 = 26, struck out ; the first expression worked in order, giving 3

marks.d2: the steps 23 − 10 = 13 and 13 × 2 = 26 are written in the bubble
marks.d3: the bubble is struck out and 10 × 2 = 20 is written beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='d1'/>Keeko thinks we work left to right, because that is how we read.
<bookmark mark='d2'/>That gives twenty three minus ten, which is thirteen, and then thirteen times two is twenty six.
<bookmark mark='d3'/>But multiplication comes first, so ten times two is twenty, and that is taken from twenty three.
